records.draft:
Hi Hanna,

Great question! You can archive your finished project in just a few clicks, and yes, you can bring it back anytime if needed.

To archive the project:
1. Go to Projects and open the project you want to archive.
2. Click Settings > Archive project.
3. Confirm the action in the dialog.
4. The project will disappear from your active project list and move to Projects > Archived.

Once archived, the project becomes read-only (no one can create, edit, or delete tasks), but you can still view it and all its tasks. Since you're an Admin, you have the permissions needed to do this.

If you need to bring it back later, just go to Projects > Archived, find the project, click the three-dot menu next to its name, and select Restore. The project will return to your active list with everything intact.

Archiving won't delete any data, and archived projects don't count toward your plan limits, so this should help with the performance issue you mentioned with the large task list.

Let us know if you have any other questions!

Quillstack Support

The draft addresses both questions: how to archive and whether it can be restored. All factual claims trace to the retrieved chunks, and the draft cites kb-0015. The customer's concern about 4000 tasks slowing things down is acknowledged, though the draft could have mentioned the 5,000 open task limit from the key facts as relevant context. However, this is a minor omission rather than an error.

Hi Oscar,

Thanks for reaching out. I found a troubleshooting step that may help: according to our documentation, TOTP codes are time-based, and even a few minutes of clock drift can cause codes to fail. You've already confirmed your phone clock is synced, which is great. The next step to try is entering the next code that appears after the current one refreshes—sometimes the server and client can be slightly out of sync, and using the next code in the sequence resolves it.

If that doesn't work, please try signing out completely and signing back in to ensure you're on a fresh session.

If codes continue to be rejected after trying these steps, a support engineer will investigate whether there's a server-side issue with your account's 2FA validation. We'll follow up on this ticket as soon as we have more information.

Quillstack Support

Hi Zara,

Thanks for reaching out! You're exactly right—that charge is a prorated amount for the seat you added on September 15th.

Here's how proration works: On the Team plan, each seat costs $12 per month. When you add a seat mid-cycle, you're charged only for the days remaining in your current billing cycle. According to your account, there were 12 days remaining when you added the seat, which resulted in the $4.80 charge.

The new seat will be billed at the full $12 monthly rate starting with your next billing cycle.

Your charge (ID ch_f24f5875cdf1) is confirmed in our system.

Let me know if you have any other questions!

Quillstack Support
